what: Chipotle Mexican Grill runs around 3,800 burrito restaurants, almost all company-owned rather than franchised. Food is cooked in each restaurant daily, and a large share of orders come through its app for collection from a second service line.
customers: Mostly younger, urban and suburban customers in the United States, with small operations in Canada and Europe.
moat: A brand built on fresh preparation that competitors with frozen supply chains cannot easily copy, and unit economics strong enough to fund rapid new-restaurant building from cash flow.
risks: Same-store transaction growth turned negative as lower-income customers cut back
Food-borne illness incidents have badly damaged the brand before
Beef and avocado costs are volatile
It pays no dividend and trades at a high multiple of earnings
opportunities: Return on invested capital of 19% is strong for a restaurant company
It is still only a third of the way to its long-term US restaurant target
Automation of preparation work could lift restaurant margins
watch: Same-store transaction growth and new restaurant openings.
